title: Teen was 'running' when officer shot him
article: Jeffrey Reodica was unarmed and running away from a Toronto police officer when he was shot three times in the back, a coroner's inquest was told yesterday.
"I just see Jeffrey's back. He's running. He's going," Brian La France said yesterday at an inquiry into the May 21, 2004, shooting death of the 17-year-old.
Mr. La France, 42, had been standing on his veranda, about 35 metres away, when he saw the teen fall onto the grass after the "pop, pop, pop" sounds of three gunshots.
He cried twice during his testimony as five jurors and about 20 observers, including Mr. Reodica's parents and Police Chief Bill Blair, looked on.
Another witness testified, however, that it looked like Mr. Reodica struck the officer on the leg before he was killed.

The shooting occurred after three youths fled from a mob of teenagers, some of them armed with baseball bats, through a Scarborough neighborhood. The chase had petered out by the time two plainclothes officers showed up in front of 75 Benleigh Dr.
The Ontario Special Investigations Unit found Detective Constable Dan Belanger used reasonable force when he shot Mr. Reodica, because the youth was swinging a knife.
But Mr. La France said he didn't see a knife. And when the teen swung his arm, it looked as if he was trying to shake off the burly police officer.
He also didn't hear the man identify himself as a police officer. As the teen ran, he heard the officer shout, "Freeze. Get back here!" before the shots rang out.
Mr. La France said that in the two years since the shooting, he hasn't talked about the incident or listened to media reports because "I wanted to keep it in my mind without it being polluted."
Another witness, Ken Tomlin, testified he saw Det. Constable Belanger take three steps backward, holding his leg as if he'd been hit.
However, Mr. Tomlin, 47, said his view of Jeffrey was blocked by the officer's back, and he didn't see the teen strike the officer. He also didn't see any knife.
Chief Blair sat through some of the proceedings.
"I'm here to show support for the police officers and to the [Reodica]family," the chief said.
He would not comment on the evidence put before the jury.
